title: Microsoft Teams: pop out the sign language interpreter video in meetings
summary: Hold: the advice to check Mode for IP video omits Microsoft's explicit exclusion of GCC, GCC High and DoD, all of which this briefing covers. The roadmap facts, interpreter-video control path and PowerShell command are supported; feature-specific controls and licensing details remain unpublished.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1]; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The accessibility guide ties the IP video meeting-policy setting to interpreters sharing a video feed.
claims.quote: Give sign language interpreters the ability to share IP video feed during Microsoft Teams meetings so they can communicate with users who are deaf or hard of hearing.

claims.claim: Mode for IP video controls outgoing and incoming meeting/group-call video and should be checked for hosts across the briefing's scope.
claims.quote: This setting isn't available for Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), GCC High, or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.
claims.fix: After the sentence describing Mode for IP video, add: 'Mode for IP video is not available in GCC, GCC High or DoD environments.' Replace the final clause beginning 'so check they are on' with 'so check IP video for the policies that interpreters' hosts use; where Mode for IP video is available, check that it is set to Outgoing and incoming video enabled.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the pop-out specifically depends on IP video or Mode for IP video.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams sign language interpreter pop out window meeting admin policy default licensing PowerShell; "sign language" "pop" "Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy". Read accessibility and audio/video policy guides; neither discusses the pop-out's specific dependency.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: IP video is reached in Teams admin center through Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Audio & video > IP video.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings, and then select Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify. Go to the Audio & video section. Check that IP video is turned On, then select Save.
claims.fix: In Governance guidance, expand the abbreviated parenthetical path to 'Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Audio & video > IP video', matching controls[1].ui. The table path itself needs no change.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowIPVideo $true enables video sharing under that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>]; [-AllowIPVideo <Boolean>]. Determines whether video is enabled in a user's meetings or calls. Set this to TRUE to allow the user to share their video.

claims.claim: The accessibility guide labels the setting IP video, while the audio/video reference lists Mode for IP video and Video conferencing.
claims.quote: Go to the Audio & video section and select the values (described in the following sections) you want for Mode for IP audio, Mode for IP video, Video conferencing, Media rate (Kbps), and Participants can use video effects.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to users and control meeting features for the users holding the policy.
claims.quote: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.

claims.claim: The accessibility guide itself does not name an administrator role requirement for these steps.
claims.quote: Searched: read accessibility-guide-admin in full for role requirements. It addresses the Microsoft Teams administrator and gives meeting-policy steps but names no specific role requirement.

claims.claim: Feature-specific user and role eligibility has not been documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams sign language interpreter popout window placement identity web mobile eligibility; "sign language" "pop-out" Teams licensing. Read accessibility guide, service description and roadmap; no pop-out user or role eligibility found.
